items.text: Explain the three fundamental drivers of AWS cost: compute, storage, and outbound data transfer
Describe the difference between On-Demand, Reserved, Spot, and Dedicated pricing models
Identify which EC2 pricing model is appropriate for a given workload scenario
Explain the six AWS Well-Architected Framework pillars and where Cost Optimization fits
Describe at least five S3 storage classes and when to use each
Explain how S3 Lifecycle Policies automate cost optimization for data tiering
Use the AWS Pricing Calculator to estimate the monthly cost of an EC2 + RDS + S3 architecture
Compare On-Demand vs. 1-year Reserved vs. 3-year Reserved costs for the same instance in the Pricing Calculator
Navigate AWS Cost Explorer to identify the top spending services and regions
Access Trusted Advisor and review the Cost Optimization category for recommendations
Identify at least three specific cost-saving actions for EC2, S3, and RDS in a given scenario
Answer questions about which pricing model offers up to 72% savings (Reserved Instances)
Identify Spot Instances as appropriate for fault-tolerant, interruptible batch workloads
Distinguish between AWS Pricing Calculator (pre-deployment), Trusted Advisor (audit), and Cost Explorer (analysis)
State all six pillars of the Well-Architected Framework correctly
Identify Dedicated Hosts as the most expensive EC2 option and explain why they're needed
